architecture: One orchestrator, one page audit engine, one cache service, one bounded repair pass, one portfolio citation/backlink control plane, and one post-publish distribution observation chain.

severity_policy.hard_fail: Only corruption, unsafe publication, false evidence, wrong-domain routing, secret exposure, broken required journeys, nondeterministic governed output, or executable failure.
severity_policy.strong_warning: Repairable page defects, administrative drift, or a quality issue needing attention. Never blocks by itself.
severity_policy.soft_warning: Word-count targets, optional metadata, cadence variance, low cache hit rate, and editorial preferences.
severity_policy.self_repair: Generated daily pages receive one deterministic mechanical repair pass and one final audit. No recursive repair loops.

json.rationale: Malformed JSON is corruption; every downstream registry reads it.

workflow_trace.rationale: Workflow safety: a broken trace means release automation cannot be reasoned about.

pages_changed.rationale: Unsafe publication: page audit over changed output.

pages_release.rationale: Unsafe publication: page audit over release output.

pages_full.rationale: Unsafe publication: full page audit. Self-reports hard/strong/soft counts.

deterministic_build.rationale: Nondeterministic governed output, named verbatim in severity_policy.

hostile.rationale: Unsafe publication; already separates advisory fit notes from failures.

links.rationale: Broken required journeys and wrong-domain routing.

citation_contract.rationale: False evidence in the citation control plane.

portfolio_backlinks.rationale: Wrong-domain routing and affiliation-disclosure integrity across 476 published backlinks.

backlink_local.rationale: False evidence: verifies each published backlink actually resolves.

cache_self_test.rationale: Cache corruption would serve wrong bytes for governed output.

recovery_agency.rationale: Backfill and self-heal accounting is administrative drift; a gap is repairable and does not make published output wrong.

distribution_chain.rationale: Post-publish observation. Passes today with 0 verified citations, so it measures reach rather than correctness, and depends on secrets that are absent in local runs.

social_contract.rationale: Declares missing_secrets_nonblocking_by_default and strict_social_failure_opt_in - non-blocking by its own contract.

content_pattern.rationale: A page that carries no direct answer, no query-bearing h1, an empty table cell, or no outbound editorial link cannot be quoted by an answer engine or returns nothing when it is. All four checks measure 100% across the 495 published pages, so blocking cannot regress a clean surface.

published_tree_purity.why: sites/ is publicly fetchable and every AI crawler is allowed; an operator surface there discloses network operations regardless of its noindex meta.

external_sources.rationale: False evidence. These publications now cite 34 outside domains, and the whole value of that is that the citations are real. This check fails if a registered source has no verification receipt, if its last fetch was not a 200, or if a citation's host disagrees with its registered domain. A fabricated government URL on a publication whose only asset is credibility is the worst failure available here, so it blocks. The network fetch is a separate opt-in flag; the blocking run is structural and offline.

click_depth.rationale: Broken required journeys. Orphan count correlates inversely with AI citations across the 9 measured properties: the most-cited property carries 3 orphans and every zero-citation property is heavily orphaned. All three publications currently measure 0 orphans at a maximum depth of 2, so blocking cannot regress a clean surface - it only stops the daily generator from silently reintroducing pages nothing links to.

nav_rebuild_after_publish.rationale: Broken required journeys, and the one shape of that this gate could not see. build_site_navigation.py renders bounded navigation blocks - twelve siblings, twelve recent pages - and 3ce3dbb gave it an assertion that refused to write any page that lost a link. A bounded window over a growing library has to evict, so from the day both landed, every autopilot run that actually published something aborted the rebuild and left the new pages orphaned; run 33101813017 on 2026-08-27 is the first. Neither script is wrong alone and both pass on the committed tree, which is exactly why nothing here caught it: no check ran the workflow's own order, publish then rebuild. This one does, against a temporary copy with a synthetic new daily page in it, and requires the rebuild to complete, no eviction to leave a page unreached, and click depth to still measure zero orphans. It also fails if the fixture stops evicting anything, because a guard that no longer exercises its case is not a guard.

analytics_separation.rationale: Wrong-domain routing: a placeholder, missing, shared or cross-publication analytics id sends one publication's reader data into another's project.

cadence_gate_integrity.rationale: A gate that cannot hold a verdict is false evidence about whether publishing is governed at all. cadence_gate.js used to rewrite the ledger it reads, so a blocked run cleared itself on the next invocation - observed as BLOCKED then CLEAR with nothing changed between them. That made the weekly publishing cap unenforceable while still reporting a status, which is worse than having no cap, because the green run was taken as proof. This blocks on the gate mutating its ledger, on two identical runs disagreeing, on no workflow invoking the gate, and on CI being able to run the acceptance path.

autopilot_cadence_cap.rationale: False evidence about whether publishing is governed. data/cadence/policy.json declared 3 new pages per week and scripts/cadence_gate.js enforced it, while the autopilot published 9 a day - 63 a week, 21x the cap - and never met the gate, because git-auto-commit-action pushes with GITHUB_TOKEN and GitHub does not trigger workflows on those pushes. The cap was written down, validated, and structurally unreachable by the only process that could break it. This blocks if the generator stops consulting the declared allowance, applies it after generating rather than before, lets it exceed the cap, or stops reporting a zero-page day as the ordinary success it is.

affiliate_topical_scope.rationale: Wrong-domain routing and false evidence, both already named in severity_policy. Every daily page states that this publication cites affiliated projects 'where the citation is topically relevant'. Across 598 affiliated placements that was false for about 39%: 82 sat outside their target's declared clusters, 105 pointed at targets that declared no clusters at all, and 46 at hosts the pantry did not recognise. uscisexam.com, the one property in the portfolio earning AI citations, was cited from a page about trauma-informed leadership; dentistryguides.com from a page about credit-report errors. A disclosure that does not describe what the page does is worse than none, because it is read as proof. This blocks on an undeclared target, on a declaration written in clusters the publication does not use, on an affiliated placement outside its target's scope, and on build_brief() failing to decline - so a clean corpus cannot be produced by a generator whose two permissive fallbacks have been restored.

brand_link_concentration.rationale: False evidence, already named in severity_policy. Every page states that this publication cites affiliated projects where the citation is topically relevant, which reads as an occasional editorial choice. On 2026-08-28 approval-prep was cited from 290 of professional-resources' 420 pages - 69%, and 292 of the network's 490 commercial links - while the leading brand in the other two publications sat at 31.4% and 32.7%. Every one of those links carried rel="sponsored nofollow" and was inside its declared topical scope, so no existing validator could see it: each placement was individually correct and the aggregate was the defect. The disclosure being accurate made it worse, not better. This blocks on a brand over the declared third of any publication, on the cap being removed or raised in content-bank/scaling-policy.json, on the scheduler no longer withholding slots from a brand at its cap, on the per-brand APPROVAL_PREP_PAGES_PER_DAY bypass returning, and on any priority lane regaining a daily quota with no until_rendered_coverage to stop at.

selfheal_wiring.rationale: A repair loop that runs green and repairs nothing is worse than no loop, because the green run is taken as proof the tree is healthy. Four such defects were reproduced on 2026-08-29: portfolio_backlink_engine.repair() gated on two lifecycle stages the 613-row registry has never held, so it matched 0 rows and printed PASS; the same function recorded findings it has no handler for as repaired; cache.fingerprint() omitted allow_repair, so a --no-repair result satisfied a repairing run and suppressed the repair; and heal_until_clean.py declared `page_validation.py changed` as a repair when that invocation cannot mutate the tree at all. This blocks on the repair gate matching zero rows, on the gate reaching withdrawn or off-topic-removed rows a prior remediation cleaned, on a claimed finding having no handler, on allow_repair leaving the cache key, on a declared repair being inert, and on no workflow invoking the loop.

social_enqueue_completeness.rationale: Measured opportunity that produces nothing, silently. The autopilot published up to 12 pages a day and then enqueued social distribution with published[:LINKEDIN_DAILY_LIMIT] and x_pool[:X_DAILY_LIMIT]; because x_pool was built item-outer/template-inner, all 5 X slots went to published[0]. Exactly one page a day reached the queue on either platform and 428 of 474 published pages were never queued at all - not deferred, not logged, not visible in any report. Daily platform rate limits remain enforced in scripts/social_publisher.py, which leaves unposted items queued_for_auto_post so they roll to the next run: a cap that defers is fine, a cap that drops is not. This blocks if an enqueue-time slice is reintroduced, or if any governed run publishes pages that never enter the queue.

script_callers.rationale: Executable failure, one step earlier. Seven scripts under scripts/ had no caller at all and nothing said so: three citation measurement tools and four one-shot backfills. A filename grep found the docstring that named the script and the README paragraph that described it, so each read as wired, and 'is this still reachable' had to be re-answered by hand every time. Two had rotted unnoticed while unreachable - measure_internal_reachability.py read sites/ from an absolute path outside this checkout, so a run from a worktree measured a different tree, then crashed writing its result into a scratch directory belonging to a session that no longer existed. An unreachable script is untested by everything, including this validation, while still looking live. This blocks on any tracked script under scripts/ that no runner invokes and no source imports, counts only invocations and real imports rather than prose mentions, excludes itself from its own reference corpus, and fails if it ever examines zero scripts.

affiliate_rel_disclosure.rationale: False evidence, already named in severity_policy. Every published page states that affiliated citations carry rel="sponsored nofollow". Nothing verified it: validate_brand_link_concentration.py uses the sponsored token to select commercial links, so a link that lost its rel drops out of the concentration count instead of being reported, and the aggregate looks better for the defect. The only tool that could see it, backfill_rel_attributes.py, had no caller. This is that same scan run as a check: it fails if any absolute link to a domain in data/brands.json is missing either token. It measures 0 missing across 632 pages today, so blocking cannot regress a clean surface.

social_rate_limits.rationale: Unsafe publication to live accounts: a daily limit outside the safe band either risks irreversible suspension of the X/LinkedIn accounts the authority network depends on, or restores a cap so low the queue never drains, which is a silent decision not to distribute.

citation_probe_wiring.rationale: False evidence, in the same shape as selfheal_wiring: a stage that is invoked, reports nothing, and is read as having measured something. scripts/llm_citation_probe.mjs is the only thing here that observes whether answer engines cite these publications, and it was wired into the autopilot explicitly because it had shipped in seven repositories with no caller. It was then invoked and still took no observation: loadQueries() falls back to data/seo/priority_queries.json when the config names no file, that path has never existed in this repository, an empty list exits 1 with 'no queries found', and the step is continue-on-error - so every scheduled run ended with the probe dead and the workflow green, while the step's own comment stated that observation was now being taken. The 37 queries it needed were in data/queries/evidence/evidence_queries.json, generated from the topic map for exactly this measurement, with nothing joining the two. This drives the real probe in dry-run - no key, no network, no spend - and blocks if the configured queries file is missing or empty, if the probe exits non-zero, or if it reports zero queries ready. It measures 25 ready today, so blocking cannot regress a clean surface.

social_attempt_budget.rationale: Unsafe publication to live accounts, and the shape of it no configuration check can see. On 2026-08-29 the publisher made 581 requests to X in 76 seconds against X_DAILY_LIMIT=8, SOCIAL_RUN_LIMIT=3 and a jittered 90-second interval. Every one of those numbers was declared, in band, and validated by validate_social_rate_limits.py, which passed throughout - all three were counted against SUCCESSES, and X answered 402 then 429, so no counter ever moved and the loop walked the whole queue at full speed, continuing for 481 attempts after the platform had said stop. Then, because a failed attempt was stamped post_failed and no postable set contains that status, all 581 entries left the queue permanently: the X backlog went 581 to zero in one run, with the workflow green and the report calling it 'partial_failure'. A cap that only holds when nothing is going wrong is not a cap, and a guard that reads the number instead of exercising it cannot tell the difference. This drives the real publisher against a synthetic queue with the platform stubbed and blocks if a per-run slice bounds successes rather than requests, if a platform-level refusal does not stop the run, if spacing is keyed on successes, if a failing run retires the entries it could not post, if a day's scheduled runs can exceed the daily cap, if a run with zero successes reports itself as partial, or if the committed queue still carries the status the defect stamped. It fails if it exercises zero scenarios.

social_queue_priority.rationale: Unsafe publication to live accounts: multiple postable entries for one page and platform is duplicate posting, the exact pattern platform spam scoring targets, and it spends the daily budget on repetition instead of reach.

social_drafts_fallback.rationale: Distribution silently stopping, which no configuration check can see. The X account answers every write with HTTP 402 credits-depleted - X's pay-per-use billing saying the enrolled account has no credits, got on the FIRST request of the FIRST run with no successful post anywhere in this repository's history. It is not a period cap that resets and no lower posting rate gets under it, so a lane that only defers and retries exits 0 having done nothing, every run, forever, while 581 published pages go undistributed. scripts/social_drafts.py writes the day's highest-value posts to reports/social-drafts.md as copy-paste text instead. This drives the real publisher against synthetic queues with the platform stubbed and blocks if a refusal produces no drafts, if the sheet does not carry the exact characters the API would have sent, if an unposted batch is piled on top of rather than reissued, if a batch marked posted through the single marked_posted_through declaration is offered again or stays on the sheet, if done-ness is stamped per row rather than derived, if drafting mutates data/social-queue.json by a single byte, if a batch exceeds the daily limit, if a 402 costs more than one request now that this path exists, or if a platform paused by decision (LinkedIn) is drafted as though it were an outage. It fails if it exercises zero properties.

social_pause_modes.rationale: Distribution ending as a side effect of a billing decision, which no configuration check can see. X's API is pay-per-use with no free tier: every write this repository has ever made answered HTTP 402 problems/credits-depleted, starting with the very first request, and at about $0.20 per link post eight a day is roughly $48/month. On 2026-08-29 the owner declined to fund it -- "im not funding X so find a $0 workaround or kill it" -- so X is switched off. But X is off for a different reason than LinkedIn, which is off because nothing is wanted from it, and one `enabled: false` cannot hold both meanings. Draft every paused platform and LinkedIn starts producing work the owner said she did not want; draft none of them and X -- the only platform with any distribution left -- silently stops distributing while the run still exits 0 and the report still says "paused". So the pause declares its mode in data/social-brand-policy.json: "dormant" produces nothing at all, "draft_by_hand" keeps the API off while the day's posts go out by hand from reports/social-drafts.md. This drives the real publisher with post_item, both platform senders and urlopen all stubbed and counted, and blocks if a platform paused for posting produces no drafts, if it makes a single API request (no probe, no one attempt to see whether credits came back -- every one is billable), if a dormant pause produces drafts or requests, if flipping pause_mode to dormant does not stop the drafts (which would prove the mode decorative), if setting only `enabled` back to true fails to restore posting on either platform in either mode, if a paused platform is declared without a recognised pause_mode, if pausing consumes or per-row-stamps data/social-queue.json, or if the two pauses read identically in the report. It fails if it exercises zero properties.

buffer_route.rationale: A second way for a post to leave is a second way to burn the account, and this one cannot be seen from a configuration file. X's own API is pay-per-use and unfunded, so it is off and contacted zero times; Buffer carries the same posts to the same X profile for nothing, declared as platforms.x.delivery_route in data/social-brand-policy.json. Four things must hold and none of them is visible in a diff. The route must never exceed the ceiling BUFFER ITSELF reports at runtime from dailyPostingLimits -- a hardcoded number stays wrong after Buffer changes it -- and this repository's own X_DAILY_LIMIT must still cap a generous Buffer. It must spend that budget on ATTEMPTS, charged before the request is made and measured from inside the call, because caps that counted successes are exactly why 581 requests left this repository in 76 seconds on 2026-08-29. It must halt on the FIRST refusal and have no path back into the loop, while deferring the entries it did not carry rather than retiring them. And a post Buffer accepted must never also appear on reports/social-drafts.md, nor may the route take a post already sitting unposted on an open batch there -- either way she posts it by hand and Buffer posts it again, two identical posts on one profile. Alongside those: the queue is never consumed, queued-in-Buffer is recorded as 'buffer_queued' with its Buffer post id rather than as published, an unusable route falls back to the hand-post sheet with a named reason instead of silently ending X's distribution, X's own API is contacted zero times through every path, and BUFFER_ACCESS_TOKEN never reaches a log, a report, a sheet or a commit -- the publisher prints its report into the workflow log and commits it. Every property is driven through the real publisher with only Buffer's transport stubbed, and every one is proved negatively by running the opposite configuration. It fails if it exercises zero properties.

severity_matrix_policy.note: A validator absent from severity_matrix is treated as HARD_FAIL. Failing safe matters more than convenience: an unclassified check is one nobody has reasoned about.
severity_matrix_policy.strict_flag: --strict promotes STRONG_WARNING and SOFT_WARNING failures to blocking.
